# Marketing-Llama-3.3-70B

Fine-tuned Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on a curated marketing instruction
dataset using AutoScientist for the AutoScientist Challenge 2026 — Marketing Category.

## Model Details

### Model Description

Marketing-Llama-3.3-70B is a LoRA fine-tuned version of
Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, adapted for marketing copy generation across
five task types: ad/social copy, email marketing, product descriptions,
brand voice rewriting, and campaign data insights.

This is part of the Marketing-Mixtral/Llama series for the AutoScientist
Challenge. The base model (Llama-3.3-70B) was selected by AutoScientist's
recipe recommendation when trained on an expanded 13,000-row dataset.
Sibling models, [Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v2](https://huggingface.co/suehuynh/Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v2), [Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3](https://huggingface.co/suehuynh/Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3), was trained on a subset of this data (8,000 rows) on Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct
for comparison (87% win rate).

- **Developed by:** Sue Huynh
- **Model type:** Causal LM, LoRA fine-tuned
- **Language:** English
- **License:** Llama 3.3 Community License
- **Finetuned from:** meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
- **Training platform:** AutoScientist by Adaption Labs

### Model Sources

- **Dataset:** suehuynh/marketing-instruct-13k
- **Related model:** [Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3](https://huggingface.co/suehuynh/Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3)
  (8K-row subset of this dataset, Mixtral-8x7B base, 87% win rate)
- **Challenge:** AutoScientist Challenge 2026 — adaptionlabs.ai

## Uses

### Direct Use

Generate marketing copy from structured briefs across five task types:

- **Ad/Social copy:** platform-specific ads with audience and CTA constraints
- **Email marketing:** campaign, lifecycle, and transactional emails with
  subject + preview + body format
- **Product descriptions:** grounded in provided attribute lists only
- **Brand voice rewriting:** neutral copy rewritten to match a specified voice
- **Table-to-insight:** campaign performance data summarized with recommendations

### Out-of-Scope Use

- Not intended for strategy generation, market research, or competitive analysis
- Not suitable for medical, legal, or financial copywriting without additional fine-tuning
- Product descriptions should always be reviewed for factual accuracy before publication
- Subject to Meta's Llama 3.3 Community License Agreement — review usage
  restrictions before commercial deployment

## Bias, Risks, and Limitations

- Training data is primarily English-language and Western marketing contexts
- Despite faithfulness-filtering on product description examples, all
  generated copy should be human-reviewed before publication
- Generated copy should not be published without editorial review
- As a 70B model, inference requires significantly more compute than the
  sibling Mixtral-8x7B model (~13B active parameters); consider the
  Mixtral version for resource-constrained deployment

### Recommendations

Always review generated copy before publication. For product descriptions,
verify all claims against the original product specification.

## How to Get Started with the Model

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from peft import PeftModel
import torch

base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="auto",
    load_in_4bit=True,
)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, "suehuynh/Marketing-Llama-3.3-70B")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct")

prompt = "Write a product description for an online store listing..."
inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt"
).to(model.device)

output = model.generate(inputs, max_new_tokens=200, do_sample=False)
print(tokenizer.decode(output[0][inputs.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

**Note:** Llama 3.3 is a gated model. Request access at
[meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct)
before loading.

## Training Details

### Training Data

13,000 examples across 5 marketing task types: the 8,000-row dataset
used for the Mixtral sibling model, plus an additional 4,000 product
description examples. See
[suehuynh/marketing-instruct-13k](https://huggingface.co/datasets/suehuynh/marketing-instruct-13k)
for full documentation.

### Training Procedure

#### Training Hyperparameters

- **Training regime:** bf16 mixed precision
- **Algorithm:** LoRA (Supervised Fine-Tuning)
- **LoRA rank:** 64
- **LoRA alpha:** 128
- **LoRA dropout:** 0
- **Target modules:** all-linear
- **Learning rate:** 1e-4
- **LR scheduler:** cosine, warmup ratio 0.05
- **Epochs:** 1
- **Weight decay:** 0.01
- **Gradient clipping:** 1.0
- **Train on inputs:** false

This recipe was recommended by AutoScientist's automatic configuration
based on the dataset characteristics; the base model (Llama-3.3-70B,
rather than Mixtral-8x7B used in earlier iterations) was also an
AutoScientist recommendation for this dataset size and composition.

#### Speeds, Sizes, Times

- **Training platform:** AutoScientist by Adaption Labs
- **Base model size:** 70B parameters

## Evaluation

### Testing Data, Factors & Metrics

#### Testing Data

Evaluated on AutoScientist's held-out internal marketing test set
(not publicly available).

#### Metrics

**Win rate:** pairwise LLM-as-judge comparison between finetuned model
output and base Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct output on identical prompts.

### Results

| Metric | Base Llama 3.3 | Finetuned | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Win rate (AS eval) | 12% | 88% | +633% relative |

#### Summary

This model achieves an 88% win rate against base Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
on AutoScientist's held-out marketing test set, trained on the largest
and most diverse dataset in this series (13,000 rows). Because the
dataset, base model, and LoRA rank all changed simultaneously relative
to the sibling Mixtral model, this result should be read as the
strongest overall outcome in the series rather than an isolated
ablation — see Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v2's model card for a controlled,
single-variable finding on the effect of epoch count.

## Environmental Impact

- **Hardware:** AutoScientist cloud infrastructure
- **Cloud Provider:** Adaption Labs

## Technical Specifications

### Model Architecture and Objective

- **Base:** Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (dense transformer)
- **Adaptation:** LoRA adapters on all linear layers
- **Objective:** Supervised fine-tuning on marketing instruction data

## Citation

**BibTeX:**
```bibtex
@misc{huynh2026marketingllama,
  author = {Huynh, Nguyen},
  title = {Marketing-Llama-3.3-70B: A Fine-tuned Model for Marketing Copy Generation},
  year = {2026},
  publisher = {HuggingFace},
  howpublished = {\url{https://huggingface.co/suehuynh/Marketing-Llama-3.3-70B}},
  note = {AutoScientist Challenge 2026 — Marketing Category}
}
```

## Model Card Authors

Sue Huynh — Brown University MSc Data Science

# Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3

Fine-tuned Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 on a curated marketing instruction
dataset using AutoScientist for the AutoScientist Challenge 2026 — Marketing Category.

## Model Details

### Model Description

Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3 is a LoRA fine-tuned version of
Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1, adapted for marketing copy generation across
five task types: ad/social copy, email marketing, product descriptions,
brand voice rewriting, and campaign data insights.

This is the second iteration of the Marketing-Mixtral series, trained on
an expanded 8,000-row dataset (up from the original 4,300 rows used in
[Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B v1](https://huggingface.co/suehuynh/Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B)).

- **Developed by:** Sue Huynh
- **Model type:** Causal LM, LoRA fine-tuned
- **Language:** English
- **License:** Apache 2.0
- **Finetuned from:** mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1
- **Training platform:** AutoScientist by Adaption Labs

### Model Sources

- **Dataset:** suehuynh/marketing-instruct-8k
- **Related model:** [Marketing-Llama-3.3-70B](https://huggingface.co/suehuynh/Marketing-Llama-3.3-70B)
  (trained on an extended 13K version of this dataset, 88% win rate)
- **Challenge:** AutoScientist Challenge 2026 — adaptionlabs.ai

## Uses

### Direct Use

Generate marketing copy from structured briefs across five task types:

- **Ad/Social copy:** platform-specific ads with audience and CTA constraints
- **Email marketing:** campaign, lifecycle, and transactional emails with
  subject + preview + body format
- **Product descriptions:** grounded in provided attribute lists only
- **Brand voice rewriting:** neutral copy rewritten to match a specified voice
- **Table-to-insight:** campaign performance data summarized with recommendations

### Out-of-Scope Use

- Not intended for strategy generation, market research, or competitive analysis
- Not suitable for medical, legal, or financial copywriting without additional fine-tuning
- Product descriptions should always be reviewed for factual accuracy before publication

## Bias, Risks, and Limitations

- Training data is primarily English-language and Western marketing contexts
- Despite faithfulness-filtering on product description examples, all
  generated copy should be human-reviewed before publication
- Generated copy should not be published without editorial review

### Recommendations

Always review generated copy before publication. For product descriptions,
verify all claims against the original product specification.

## How to Get Started with the Model

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from peft import PeftModel
import torch

base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="auto",
    load_in_4bit=True,
)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, "suehuynh/Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1")

prompt = "Write a product description for an online store listing..."
inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt"
).to(model.device)

output = model.generate(inputs, max_new_tokens=200, do_sample=False)
print(tokenizer.decode(output[0][inputs.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

## Training Details

### Training Data

8,000 examples across 5 marketing task types — an expansion of the
original 4,300-row dataset with additional sources for table-to-insight,
email marketing, and ad copy/brand voice. See
[suehuynh/marketing-instruct-8k](https://huggingface.co/datasets/suehuynh/marketing-instruct-8k)
for full documentation.

### Training Procedure

#### Training Hyperparameters

- **Training regime:** bf16 mixed precision
- **Algorithm:** LoRA (Supervised Fine-Tuning)
- **LoRA rank:** 32
- **LoRA alpha:** 64
- **LoRA dropout:** 0.05
- **Target modules:** all-linear
- **Learning rate:** 1.5e-4
- **LR scheduler:** cosine, warmup ratio 0.05
- **Epochs:** 1
- **Weight decay:** 0.01
- **Gradient clipping:** 1.0
- **Train on inputs:** false

**Note on epochs:** an earlier run on this identical dataset and recipe
with `n_epochs=3` achieved an 83% win rate. Changing only `n_epochs` to 1
(holding every other hyperparameter constant) improved the win rate to
87% — a controlled, single-variable result indicating that additional
training epochs on this dataset size leads to overfitting and reduced
generalization against the base model judge.

#### Speeds, Sizes, Times

- **Training platform:** AutoScientist by Adaption Labs
- **Base model size:** 46.7B parameters (Mixtral MoE, ~13B active per token)

## Evaluation

### Testing Data, Factors & Metrics

#### Testing Data

Evaluated on AutoScientist's held-out internal marketing test set
(not publicly available).

#### Metrics

**Win rate:** pairwise LLM-as-judge comparison between finetuned model
output and base Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct output on identical prompts.

### Results

| Metric | Base Mixtral | Finetuned | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Win rate (AS eval) | 13% | 87% | +569% relative |

#### Summary

This model achieves an 87% win rate against base Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct
on AutoScientist's held-out marketing test set, up from 80% in v1
(trained on 4,300 rows, 1 epoch).

The most notable finding from this iteration is a controlled,
single-variable experiment: on the same 8,000-row dataset with an
identical recipe, training for 3 epochs produced 83% win rate, while
training for 1 epoch (with no other change) produced 87%. This
isolates epoch count as a direct driver of overfitting at this
dataset size — more passes over the data degrade generalization
against the base model judge rather than improving it.

## Environmental Impact

- **Hardware:** AutoScientist cloud infrastructure
- **Cloud Provider:** Adaption Labs

## Technical Specifications

### Model Architecture and Objective

- **Base:** Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 (Mixture of Experts, 8 experts, 2 active per token)
- **Adaptation:** LoRA adapters on all linear layers
- **Objective:** Supervised fine-tuning on marketing instruction data

## Citation

**BibTeX:**
```bibtex
@misc{huynh2026marketingmixtralv3,
  author = {Huynh, Nguyen},
  title = {Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3: A Fine-tuned Model for Marketing Copy Generation},
  year = {2026},
  publisher = {HuggingFace},
  howpublished = {\url{https://huggingface.co/suehuynh/Marketing-Mixtral-8x7B-v3}},
  note = {AutoScientist Challenge 2026 — Marketing Category}
}
```

## Model Card Authors

Sue Huynh — Brown University MSc Data Science

## Model Card Contact

# Gemma-4 KJV Bible Instruct

Gemma-4 KJV Bible Instruct is a domain-specialized large language model fine-tuned from Google's Gemma-4-E2B using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).

The model is designed to generate responses grounded in the King James Version (KJV) of the Holy Bible while maintaining the instruction-following capabilities of Gemma-4.

## Highlights

- Base Model: Gemma-4-E2B
- Fine-tuning:
  - Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
  - Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
- Framework:
  - Unsloth
  - Transformers
  - TRL
  - PEFT LoRA
- Precision:
  - 4-bit QLoRA training
  - 16-bit merged inference model
- Language:
  - English
- Domain:
  - Biblical Question Answering
  - Scripture Retrieval
  - Christian Education
  - Theological Research

## Intended Use

This model is intended for:

- Biblical study
- Scripture search
- Bible question answering
- Church education
- Personal devotion
- Research
- AI experimentation

## Out-of-Scope Uses

This model should not be used for:

- Legal advice
- Medical advice
- Financial advice
- Replacing professional theological counseling
- Generating authoritative doctrinal statements

## Dataset

Training data includes:

- King James Version (KJV)
- Curated instruction datasets
- Preference datasets for DPO alignment

## Training

Stage 1
- Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)

Stage 2
- Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

Hardware

- Tesla T4 GPUs
- Kaggle Notebooks

Frameworks

- Unsloth
- Transformers
- PEFT
- TRL
- PyTorch

## Limitations

- Optimized primarily for the King James Version.
- May hallucinate if asked about topics outside biblical content.
- Does not replace scholarly biblical interpretation.
- Responses should be verified against the original scripture.

## License

Please follow the Gemma license in addition to this repository's license.

## Citation

If you use this model in research, please cite this repository.

# Gemma-4 KJV Bible Instruct

Gemma-4 KJV Bible Instruct is a domain-adapted large language model based on Google's Gemma-4-E2B. It has been fine-tuned to provide instruction-following responses grounded in the King James Version (KJV) of the Holy Bible.

The model was trained using a two-stage alignment pipeline:

1. Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
2. Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

This combination improves instruction following while encouraging responses that remain faithful to biblical language and scripture.


## Model Details

**Base Model**
- Google Gemma-4-E2B

**Architecture**
- Decoder-only Transformer

**Fine-tuning**
- LoRA (PEFT)
- QLoRA (4-bit training)

**Alignment**
- Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

**Frameworks**
- Unsloth
- Hugging Face Transformers
- TRL
- PEFT
- PyTorch

## Intended Uses

This model is designed for:

- Biblical question answering
- Scripture explanation
- Bible study
- Christian education
- Sermon preparation assistance
- Research on instruction tuning
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

## Limitations

- Optimized primarily for the King James Version (KJV).
- May generate inaccurate or unsupported theological statements.
- Should not replace qualified pastoral or scholarly interpretation.
- Responses should always be verified against the original biblical text.

## Training Pipeline

Stage 1
- Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)

Stage 2
- Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

Training Framework
- Unsloth
- Transformers
- TRL
- PEFT

Training Hardware
- NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPUs
- Kaggle Notebooks

## Example

### Prompt

```
Explain John 3:16.
```

### Response

The verse teaches that God demonstrated His love for humanity by giving His only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, so that everyone who believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. It emphasizes God's love, salvation through faith, and the promise of eternal life.

models.description:
# Model Summary

This is a LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adapter fine-tuned on top of `google/gemma-4-31B-it`, specializing the base model for financial and quantitative reasoning. It was built and trained via Adaption Labs' Adaptive Data and AutoScientist platforms as a submission to the AutoScientist Challenge 2026 (Finance category).

The adapter targets the attention projections (q/k/v/o) of the base model and was trained via supervised fine-tuning on a combined dataset of financial reasoning examples, including multi-hop financial statement analysis (cross-period ratio comparisons), verification of 10-K MD&A narrative claims against reported financial figures, financial QA/extraction tasks over tables and disclosures, and crypto-native tokenomics reasoning restricted to spot-based instruments.

The combined training dataset improved from a quality score of 7.0 (grade C, 14.4th percentile) to 8.8 (grade A, 44.8th percentile) on Adaption's diagnostic evaluation — a 26.4% relative improvement — after platform-based data enhancement.

## Usage

Load the adapter on top of the base model using PEFT:

```python
from peft import PeftModel
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("google/gemma-4-31B-it")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/gemma-4-31B-it")
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, "oxzaid10/gemma-4-31b-financial-reasoning-lora")

prompt = "In its 10-K MD&A for fiscal year 2023, XYZ stated revenue increased due to higher product sales. Verify this claim against the company's reported financial figures."
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

**Input shape:** text prompt (string), tokenized to the base model's vocabulary, up to the base model's 256K-token context window.
**Output shape:** generated text (string) — a step-by-step reasoning trace followed by a final answer/verification statement.

**Known and preventable failures:**
- A portion of the training data's completions were elaborated by the Adaptive Data platform's own generation model. While base claims and directional labels (e.g. "revenue increased/decreased") were verified against real SEC XBRL data, some enhanced completions may include illustrative sub-figures (e.g. invented segment-level breakdowns) not independently verified against source filings. Users should not treat specific numeric figures in generated outputs as authoritative without independent verification against primary source documents.
- The model may occasionally conflate consolidated and segment/business-unit-level financial figures, a known limitation in a portion of the source training data (MD&A narrative extraction) that was filtered but not eliminated.
- The model has not been evaluated for non-English financial documents or non-US regulatory filing contexts.

## System

This is a standalone LoRA adapter, not part of a larger pipeline. It requires the base model `google/gemma-4-31B-it` to be loaded alongside it (LoRA adapters do not function independently). Input requirements: text prompts within the base model's tokenizer vocabulary and context window. Downstream dependencies: any application consuming this model's outputs should independently verify specific numeric claims before using them in a financial decision-making context, per the limitations above.

## Implementation requirements

- **Hardware:** Training was performed on Adaption Labs' AutoScientist managed compute infrastructure (specific hardware not exposed to the end user).
- **Software:** PEFT 0.15.1, standard Hugging Face Transformers-compatible training stack.
- **Compute:** LoRA fine-tuning (not full fine-tuning) — trains a small fraction of the 31B base model's parameters. Adapter file size: ~87.7 MB (`adapter_model.safetensors`). Training ran for 1 epoch.
- **Inference:** Standard inference requirements for a 31B dense transformer model (consumer GPU/workstation class, per Gemma 4's stated target deployment), plus the small additional adapter overhead.

# Model Characteristics

## Model initialization

Fine-tuned from a pre-trained model, not trained from scratch. Base model: `google/gemma-4-31B-it` (Google DeepMind's instruction-tuned 31B dense model from the Gemma 4 family). This adapter only modifies a small set of additional low-rank matrices inserted into the attention layers; the base model's pre-trained weights are unchanged and reused as-is.

## Model stats

- **Base model size:** 31B parameters (dense, all active per forward pass)
- **Adapter size:** ~87.7 MB on disk (LoRA rank 16, alpha 32)
- **Trainable parameters:** LoRA adapter only, targeting `q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj` across all attention layers — a small fraction of the base model's 31B parameters
- **Layers:** inherits base model architecture (hybrid local/global attention, dense transformer)
- **Latency:** not independently benchmarked; expect latency comparable to the base `google/gemma-4-31B-it` model plus negligible adapter overhead, since LoRA adds minimal inference-time computation

## Other details

The model is not pruned or quantized as released (adapter weights are in full precision as exported by the training platform; users may separately quantize the merged model if desired). No differential privacy techniques were applied during training. No data anonymization beyond standard public SEC filing content (which is already public record) was required, as no personal/private data was used in training.

# Data Overview

## Training data

The model was fine-tuned on the **Financial Quantitative and Crypto Dataset** (25,378 rows after platform enhancement), combining four component datasets, each built and adapted via Adaption Labs' Adaptive Data platform:

1. **financial_qa_with_reasoning**: Combines (a) multi-hop numeric reasoning rows generated by pure pandas composition over SEC XBRL financial facts for 150 curated US Mega/Large-Cap companies (no LLM involved — cross-period ratio comparisons such as margin stability vs. revenue growth, ROE/ROA leverage divergence, liquidity vs. leverage trade-offs); (b) MD&A narrative claim verification rows, where claims extracted from real 10-K Management's Discussion and Analysis sections (via a validated regex-based extraction pipeline) were checked against the company's actual reported financial figures (sourced from SEC's XBRL companyfacts API, with fiscal years resolved via real filing dates rather than inferred); and (c) supplementary financial QA/calculation examples adapted from TheFinAI/FinCoT (Hugging Face), itself combining FinQA, ConvFinQA, TAT-QA, and related sources.
2. **mda_financial_extraction**: Additional MD&A-derived extraction examples (figures cited, stated drivers, period comparisons).
3. **financial_ratio_calculation**: Additional financial ratio calculation examples.
4. **crypto_supply_metrics**: Crypto-native financial reasoning examples (circulating/max/total supply percentages, fully diluted valuation premiums) restricted to spot-based instruments.

**Collection:** Numeric data was collected directly from SEC EDGAR's XBRL `companyfacts` API. MD&A narrative text was extracted from primary 10-K filing documents (Item 7 sections). Supplementary QA data was sourced from the public TheFinAI/FinCoT dataset on Hugging Face.

**Pre-processing:** Company universe was filtered to exclude haram-adjacent sectors (banks, insurers, mortgage REITs, asset managers, derivatives exchanges) per the project's design blueprint, which also excludes interest-bearing instruments, leverage/margin trading, derivatives, prediction markets, and meme coins across all data. Revenue and other financial line items were coalesced across multiple inconsistent XBRL tag variants (e.g. pre/post-ASC-606 revenue tags, REIT-specific lease-income tags) using a per-company magnitude-consistency check to avoid mismatched tag contamination. MD&A claim extraction applied segment/business-unit/product-line/geography exclusion filters to avoid conflating sub-component figures with consolidated totals; rows with unresolved ambiguity were dropped. All raw component datasets were then passed through Adaption Labs' Adaptive Data platform for additional quality enhancement and diagnosis scoring prior to fine-tuning.

## Demographic groups

Not applicable. This dataset contains corporate financial data (company-level financial statements, SEC filings) and does not include personal or demographic data about individuals.

## Evaluation data

Train/test split was managed internally by the AutoScientist training platform (not directly configured by the model developer). Evaluation was conducted on a held-out split of the same combined dataset distribution; no notable distributional differences between training and evaluation data are known beyond standard random splitting. Adaption Labs separately maintains its own held-out in-house test sets for the Finance category, used for competition-level baseline comparison (see AutoScientist Challenge rules).

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

Training-time evaluation was tracked via AutoScientist's win-rate metric, comparing the LoRA-adapted model against the unmodified base model (`google/gemma-4-31B-it`) on the training dataset's held-out evaluation split, alongside standard train/validation loss curves, learning rate schedule, and gradient norm tracking (available on the AutoScientist training dashboard). Separately, the training data itself was evaluated by Adaptive Data's diagnostic tool, improving from a quality score of 7.0 (grade C) to 8.8 (grade A) — a 25.7-26.4% relative improvement depending on the specific dataset snapshot evaluated.

## Subgroup evaluation results

No formal subgroup analysis was performed, as the dataset does not contain demographic subgroups. An informal "subgroup" lens worth noting: the dataset spans four distinct task types (multi-hop numeric reasoning, MD&A narrative verification, general financial QA/extraction, crypto supply-metric calculation) with different generation methods (pure computation, regex-extraction, platform-generated). No per-task-type evaluation breakdown was performed; this is a known gap.

## Fairness

Fairness in the demographic sense was not a primary design consideration for this domain (corporate financial data), and no fairness metrics were computed. The more relevant "fairness" concern for this model is **company/sector representational fairness**: the underlying numeric and MD&A training data covers 150 curated US Mega/Large-Cap companies (after excluding several entire sectors per the project's design blueprint — see Ethics below), meaning the model's grounding is concentrated in large-cap, non-financial-services US equities and may generalize less reliably to small-cap companies, non-US filers, or excluded sectors (banks, insurers, REITs, asset managers).

## Usage limitations

This model should not be used for actual investment, trading, or financial advisory decisions. It has not been validated to the standard required for regulated financial use. Specific numeric figures in model outputs should always be independently verified against primary source documents (SEC filings) before being relied upon, given the known risk of platform-enhanced completions containing unverified illustrative figures (see Model Summary / Usage). The model's training data deliberately excludes interest-bearing instruments, leverage/margin trading, derivatives, prediction markets, and meme coins — it should not be expected to perform well on, and should not be used for, reasoning tasks involving those topics.

## Ethics

The training data's design deliberately excludes interest-bearing instruments (loans, bonds, interest-rate products), leverage and margin trading, derivatives (futures, options), prediction markets, and meme coins, reflecting an Islamic-finance-informed (halal) design constraint chosen by the model developer. This was treated as a data curation and blueprint constraint applied consistently across all training data components, rather than as a fairness intervention, but it does mean the model's domain coverage is narrower by design than a general-purpose financial model. A separate, identified risk is that a portion of the training data's completions were generated/enhanced by a third-party platform's own model rather than fully human- or rule-verified; this is disclosed transparently here and in the model's README so downstream users can make an informed risk assessment rather than discovering it implicitly. No other ethical risks specific to this model (e.g. CSAM, violence, generation of harmful content) were identified, as the domain (corporate financial disclosure analysis) does not naturally implicate those risk categories; the model inherits the base model's (`google/gemma-4-31B-it`) general safety training and mitigations.

instances.overview:
This is the instruction-tuned 31B dense variant of Gemma 4, Google DeepMind's latest open-weight model family, packaged for use with the Hugging Face Transformers library. Gemma 4 31B IT activates all 31 billion parameters on every forward pass (dense architecture, as opposed to the MoE 26B variant), built on the Gemini 3 architecture. It supports a 256K-token context window, multimodal input (text and image, with video handled as frame sequences), function-calling, structured JSON output, native system-prompt support, and configurable reasoning/"thinking" modes, with multilingual coverage across 140+ languages.
This instance uses a hybrid attention mechanism that interleaves local sliding-window attention with full global attention (ensuring the final layer is always global), with unified Keys and Values in global layers and Proportional RoPE (p-RoPE) to support efficient long-context performance. It is suitable for fine-tuning (e.g. via LoRA/PEFT) on domain-specific tasks, as well as direct use for reasoning, coding, agentic workflows, and multimodal understanding on consumer GPUs and workstations.
